notes: EDA v4: reviewed findings, confidence and rule-input status are in reports/eda/SUMMARY.md and tools/scene/CONTRACT.md. The notes below are automatic descriptive statistics of this clip only.
1834 tracks in 318 s: 1229 pedestrians (67%), 502 car, 35 bus, 51 truck, 12 motorcycle, 5 bicycle; 5 person boxes riding two-wheelers were relabelled as riders.
On average 33.5 pedestrians and 29 vehicles are on screen at once (peak 49 pedestrians).

4 vehicle flows found; the largest are F1 top-left to bottom-right (towards camera, left to right, 195 tracks); F2 middle-right to top-left (right to left, 186 tracks); F3 bottom-right to bottom-left (right to left, 14 tracks).

Furthest queued stop that began while head D showed red, red_amber or amber, per flow (rough upper bound for a stop line; D is a timing proxy for the near carriageway only): F1 near [3533, 1103] (47% of its vehicles stopped >= 2 s, queue 12.3 vs 3.2 vehicles while D red vs not red); F2 near [3069, 1273] (13% of its vehicles stopped >= 2 s, queue 1.3 vs 0.8 vehicles while D red vs not red); F4 near [494, 1071] (62% of its vehicles stopped >= 2 s, queue 0.7 vs 0.1 vehicles while D red vs not red).

Median pedestrian box height is 112 px at 4K; 27% are under 96px (16px at imgsz 640), 2% are under 64px (16px at imgsz 960), 1% are under 48px (16px at imgsz 1280). These are detected boxes, so the smallest people are already missing.

Mean luma goes from 69.5 to 58.3 (-16.1%) over the clip, range 57.6 to 73.4 of 255; the largest swing is -18.0% within 15 s (216 to 231 s). Iris, shutter and gain are constant in the camera metadata (reports/eda/camera), so this is not exposure control; brightness rules (fire_smoke) must still normalise per frame.

305 of 1229 pedestrian tracks spend >= 0.5 s on cells used by moving vehicles; 5 crossing corridor(s) found, the busiest spans x 2240 to 3760, y 880 to 1200 (206 people); 82 people are on the road outside corridors, most around [732, 298] (includes kerbside waiting and bus boarding, so an upper bound for jaywalking).

Signal: vehicle head D (3 lamps, from the head inventory) at (2234, 820) in this video; its v4 timeline has a known state for 95.9% of the clip (coverage, not accuracy: no human-verified labels yet). D is a timing proxy for the near-carriageway flow; which movements it controls is unknown.

Of 418 vehicle tracks with enough motion, 336 go straight, 68 turn and 8 reverse heading (U-turn like, e.g. track 824 at [1895, 877] around 37.6 s); check these by eye before treating them as illegal_u_turn examples.
6 vehicle(s) stand still for over 90% of a track longer than 60 s at [108, 1118], [1567, 554], [971, 394], [39, 957], [993, 396] (parked), which a stopped_vehicle rule must whitelist or time-gate.
Tracker: 19.9% of tracks live under 1 s and 54.8% of vehicle tracks start away from the frame edge, a sign of occlusion and ID switches.

lane_flow_clustering.method: k-means on start xy, end xy, net heading, then merge clusters that share heading (< 20 deg) and line (< 250 px)
lane_flow_clustering.rule: vehicle tracks >= 2 s and >= 300 px net travel

turning_movements.rule: heading change between first and last 5 moving samples; |d| < 35 straight, > 140 U-turn like; image-plane, so perspective bends it

signal.status: PROVISIONAL (coverage only; no human-verified lamp labels yet)
signal.box_mapping: box_ref (reference C3897 4K px) mapped with H_ref_to_video from registration.json
signal.meaning: head D is a strong timing proxy for the near-carriageway flow; the far carriageway is also cycle-locked with a different phase offset; which movements D physically controls is UNKNOWN (reports/eda/SUMMARY.md, finding 3)

perspective.assumption: person height about 1.7 m; valid only near the fitted y range

pedestrians_on_carriageway.definition: person ground point in a direction-field cell used by moving vehicles, >= 5 samples (~0.5 s)
pedestrians_on_carriageway.corridor_rule: road cells with >= 20 distinct people, dilated by one cell
